text: Seabrook Town's 3-4-3 formation enabled a decisive tactical shift at 65', increasing press intensity (press from 0.66 to 0.84), directness (0.42 to 0.57), and line height (0.6 to 0.72). This triggered enhanced field tilt to 63.3% and a reduced PPDA of 4.7 in the second half, suffocating Harbour City's patient, short-passing 4-2-3-1 style and forcing 7 turnovers after halftime[#1361]. Harbour City's first goal stemmed from a 17-pass, patient build-up culminating in a through ball assist by Marek Barros, illustrating their methodical possession approach before conceding to Seabrook's fast transitions[#904][#905]. The counter-attacking pressing trigger is epitomized by Tariq Marlowe’s immediate regain-and-finish at 53', exploiting Harbour City's disorganization following early goals[#1103][#1104]. Seabrook’s late breakthrough via Kian Romano involved rapid vertical transitions with a 7.2-second counter attack and a swift open-play sequence post-tactical change, underscoring their reliance on wing overloads and pressing traps consistent with their wide crossing play[#1881][#1882][#1905][#1906]. Despite Marek Barros' high defensive (9 interceptions) and creative outputs (2 assists), Harbour City's field tilt of only 42.3% limited their ability to stabilize possession in the closing stages[#975].

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for analyst audience in en

- Seabrook Town had a higher xG of 3.44 compared to Harbour City's 1.03, reflecting more quality chances created overall. [#1882]
- Kian Romano scored two late goals in stoppage time at 90+2' and 90+3' with high xG values of 0.605 and 0.952 respectively, turning the game in Seabrook Town's favor. [#1882, #1906]
- Harbour City scored two early goals at 45' and 47' minutes by Elias Okafor and Marek Barros, but conceded four goals in total. [#905, #975]
- Seabrook Town demonstrated greater control in the second half with 55.4% possession, 13 shots, and 3 big chances, fueling their comeback. [#1448]
- Marek Barros was player of the match with 1 goal, 2 assists, 9 interceptions, and a 9.8 rating despite his team losing. [#975]

- Seabrook Town capitalized on regains and quick transitions to score, notably Tariq Marlowe’s goal at 53’ came immediately after a regain with no passes involved, reflecting a counter-attack pattern exploiting Harbour City's momentary disorganization after their early lead [#1103,#1104].
- Harbour City’s first goal at 45’ arose from a prolonged, patient build-up (17 passes over nearly a minute) aligned with their 4-2-3-1 formation and patient short passing style, showing their emphasis on methodical possession before delivering a through ball assist by Marek Barros [#904,#905].
- The 47’ goal by Marek Barros was generated from a set piece (corner) and a long-range cross, indicating Harbour City’s capability to exploit set pieces despite their preference for short passing and a structured 4-2-3-1 shape [#973,#975].
- Seabrook Town’s tactical adjustment at 65’ to press higher, play more direct, and raise their defensive line led to increased offensive threat and more goals, demonstrating their responsiveness and reflecting their 3-4-3 formation’s flexibility to ramp up pressure and crossing opportunities later in the game [#1361,#1447,#1448].
- The late goals by Kian Romano, including an immediate counter-attack finish (a 7.2s build-up from regain) and a quick open-play move after a tactical change, underscore Seabrook Town’s effective use of pressing traps and quick verticality, consistent with their wide, crossing playstyle and formation’s emphasis on wing play [#1881,#1882,#1905,#1906].
- Harbour City’s higher turnovers, especially in the second half (7), and reduced box touches coincided with Seabrook’s growing field tilt and effective pressing (PPDA 4.7 in the second half), illustrating Seabrook’s success in disrupting Harbour City’s patient passing game and forcing errors [#team_stats].
